question: A teacher has written end-of-year report comments for every pupil in her class. The school's rule is that no comment may be pasted into Claude until the school office has confirmed that it is cleared for sharing with parents. She wants Claude to turn the cleared comments into short parent-friendly summaries, one pupil at a time, and the office wants every summary written at the same reading level and length. Which sequence should she follow when putting the request together?
options: A) Confirm which comments are cleared for sharing; paste the cleared comments, by pupil; ask for one summary per pupil, leaving the reading level and length for Claude to choose.
B) Confirm which comments are cleared for sharing; paste the cleared comments in one block, without pupil names; ask for one combined summary of the whole class, stating the reading level and length.
C) Paste every comment, by pupil; confirm which comments are cleared for sharing; ask for one summary per pupil of the cleared comments only, stating the reading level and length.
D) Confirm which comments are cleared for sharing; paste only the cleared comments, by pupil; ask for one summary per pupil, stating the reading level and length you want.
correct_answers: D) Confirm which comments are cleared for sharing; paste only the cleared comments, by pupil; ask for one summary per pupil, stating the reading level and length you want.
explanations: The clearance check comes first and only cleared comments are pasted, but the request leaves the reading level and length for Claude to choose. The office wants every summary at the same reading level and length, and Claude's prompting guidance is to be specific about the desired output format and constraints, so those requirements have to be stated in the request.

The clearance check comes first, but pasting the comments in one block without pupil names throws away the pupil-by-pupil structure, and a single combined summary of the whole class is not the one summary per pupil the teacher wants. Stating the reading level and length does not repair a request for the wrong deliverable.

Every comment, including any the office has not cleared, is pasted before the clearance check, so the school's rule is already broken. Asking Claude to use only the cleared comments afterwards does not undo that, because the rule governs what may be pasted at all.

Correct. The school's rule says nothing is pasted until the office has confirmed it is cleared, so the check comes first and only the cleared comments go in. They are organized by pupil so each summary can be tied to one pupil, and the request asks for one summary per pupil while stating the reading level and length, which gives Claude the specific output constraints the office wants. Each step follows from the rule or the task in the scenario.
